title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-04-09
lineage: [SBD > MR > Cass > D > CD] + [AUD > MC > 4x Cass > DAT > CD]

ai_review.summary: Matrix recording mixing sublime acoustic soundboard with uneven audience sections, highlighted by a thrilling Other One and the quirky Cowboy Song.
ai_review.review: The show captures an early‑1970 Fillmore West performance that swings from an excellent acoustic set into a mysterious electric jam dubbed “Cowboy Song,” with a particularly exciting The Other One.  The recording is a blend of crystal‑clear soundboard audio and decent audience pickup, though parts of the tape suffer from noticeable drop‑outs and uneven mix quality.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical moments (Other One, Cowboy Song) and give 4–5 stars, but several note serious audio flaws in portions of the tape; combined weighted score yields a solid mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Acoustic soundboard is described as sublime and clear; audience sections are acceptable but some tracks (e.g., "It's A Man's World") have audio glitches or muffled mix, making the overall recording uneven.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with a strong acoustic set that matches known setlists, then moves into an electric portion featuring the oddball Cowboy jam and a smoky first electric set; some reviewers felt later repertoire sounded bored or less inspired.
